verdicts.strengths: The geography follows the classic world map. Mushroom Town sits at the NW tip, the snail valley runs SE, the fork is at A Split Road, Southperry is to the south, Amherst is east, Field East and Tomato Field are on the SE end, and the lake and waterfall are north-centre. All 20 trails connect, with reciprocal portals (portal_topology ok). One sun, one inked-outline style and one bright saturated palette keep lighting and materials consistent across all maps. Southperry (beige stone, blue domes, palms) and Tomato Field (pergola, beds, giant tomatoes) are clear, distinct landmarks even at island scale. The island visibly floats above clouds and sea, which matches the world-map concept.
The coloured mushroom houses with spotted caps, the clean dirt main path with portals, the fenced gardens and the bluff terraces are charming and read well up close.
Good variety: a stone tower, a red-capped mushroom platform with a ladder, a stump house and wooden stair landings. The S-curving path reads clearly. It is more vertical and interesting than 10000.

Reads as a town. It has a cobbled plaza with a rainbow, a giant hollow tree, five mushroom houses (including a striped one), retaining walls with ladders and lamps. Clearly more developed than the fields around it.
The most developed map on the island. Beige sandstone plaza, blue-dome Mediterranean houses, lighthouse, market stalls, palms, crates, stairs and a full three-masted ship. Strong identity up close.
Good layering of tiers, with stone-pillar gaps, vines on the cliff faces and log props. The traversal reads clearly.
Stepping-stone pad stairs, layered grass tiers and a rainbow fountain give real vertical play and depth.
Natural tiers with a stone arch, a stepping-pad climb and a fenced paddock. It sits beside the lake, so it has a backdrop.
Spiral pad stairs, plank ramps, logs and stumps. A readable small-forest clearing with good vertical play.
A clear dirt road with fences and signs, and a raised knoll with a ladder. It connects to both branches.
The most distinctive field on the island: a tomato-arch gate, a long pergola, tomato beds, scarecrows and giant tomatoes. It is recognisable from any distance.
Flower-bed terraces in distinct colours with vines on the walls. It reads as a garden and is distinct from the hunting forests.
A stepped hillside with crops and shroom props, and a tomato-arch link to Tomato Field. The autumn palette sets it apart from the west.

issues.issue: world.py island() (lines 155-170) builds the outline as the convex hull of every footprint plus a uniform LY.ISLAND_MARGIN = 34 m (layout.py 272), with a 9 m and a 3 m wobble. Three problems follow. (a) Every map sits roughly 25-35 m inside the cliff, so no map touches the rim. Southperry (geo centre about (451,-355)) has 6-8 rows of palms and grass between its south wall and the cliff (Region_SouthperryAndSplitRoad, bottom third). (b) The silhouette is a smooth convex lozenge with no headlands or bays (Island_Overview, Island_WorldMapStyle). It does not have the chunky plateau of the reference, whose north rim extends well north of the lake. (c) The large hull fill is just filler forest.
issues.fix: Replace the hull with an authored geo-frame outline (a polygon in layout.py, about 20-30 control points, Chaikin-smoothed), or keep the hull but allow per-map, per-edge rim overrides, e.g. MAPS[60000]['rim'] = {'front': 0.0}. Give Southperry a southern headland whose cliff line runs along its dock edge (the footprint's front edge, local y = 0). Put West Entrance (0) on the NW tip with margin 0 on its west edge, and Field East/Tomato Field near the SE rim with margin of 8 m or less. Push the north rim 60-90 m north of the lake (geo y about -40) to leave room for the NE massif. Add 2-3 shallow bays (for example on the SW rim between SHG II and the fork) so the cliff line has rhythm.

issues.issue: The port is landlocked. The ship sits in a small walled basin inside a rectangular stone platform, with grass, palms and forest on every side (Southperry_60000_Overview, right third). The world map has the ship 'docked just SE of the town, over the rim', hanging beside the cliff. The lighthouse is about the height of the two-storey houses, so it is not visible in Island_Overview or Island_Hero (the plaza reads only as a beige rectangle).
issues.fix: Once the shared rim override exists, rebuild the SE quarter (local x about 60-82) as the island edge. Remove the basin's outer stone wall and grass. End the dock pier at the cliff lip and place the ship so 50-70% of its hull overhangs the void, with mooring ropes and a gangplank to the pier. Raise the lighthouse to 22-26 m with the classic cream body, gold bands, blue dome and red-orange cap so it is the tallest object in the south half. Put it on the rim corner so it silhouettes against the sea in island shots.

issues.issue: The island top is flat and every map sits on a ziggurat. Island_Ground is one flat terrace (top z = 0, bottom -18; world.py 167). Map heights span only 0-18 m over an 800 m island. All relief comes from plinth stacks (world.py plinth(), lines 129-152: 3 m steps, each level the same rounded rectangle offset another 3.6 m with wobble 1.0 + 0.4i) plus scattered cones. The result is concentric rectangular terrace stripes around every map (Region_MushroomTownArea: 6-7 parallel bands; Region_WestAmherstForests: three rectangular stepped pyramids). Map rectangles read through, and the classic 'valley between ridges' and 'Mushroom Town pocket high in the NW' geography is invisible at island scale.
issues.fix: Replace the flat Island_Ground with a designed heightfield. Displace a grid mesh in the geo frame using a height function: NW massif 40-60 m around the Mushroom Town pocket (geo x 0-120, y -40 to +60); a valley floor falling from about 25 m at map 30000 (148,-77) to about 4 m at the fork (415,-274); a raised east ridge between the valley and the lake; a NE massif north of the lake and Snail Field of Flowers; an Amherst shelf at about 8 m. Derive each map's z from the heightfield (MAPS[...]['z'] = h(centre)). Plinths then need only 1-2 tiers. Give them irregular outlines (wobble 3-5 m at freq about 0.05, not rounded rectangles), varied step heights (2-6 m) and a regional style: beige rock cliffs in the MT pocket, soft grass slopes in the valley, sandstone at Southperry.

issues.issue: The floating plateau reads as a thin pancake, not the 'sheer grey-beige cliff walls' of worldmap.md section 2. The visible wall is only the 18 m dirt band of Island_Ground. underside() (world.py 172-205) starts tapering at once (levels (-17.5,1.0), (-30,0.97), (-48,0.9), (-70,0.78)...), so at 40° pitch the taper hides behind the top surface. Cloud_CliffBase puffs at z -38 to -90 (lines 468-478) cover the rest. M_Rock_Under (materials.py 471) uses Wave BANDS with distortion 8 and renders as dark grey wood-grain or marble stripes (Region_SnailHuntingGrounds and Region_MapleRoad, lower left).
issues.fix: Make the wall sheer for 50-70 m before tapering, e.g. levels (-18,1.0), (-40,1.0), (-62,0.98), (-88,0.9), (-118,0.72), (-150,0.5), (-185,0.27), (-215,0.1), tip at about -250. Add vertical column or facet noise (high frequency in xy, stretched in z) so it reads as cliff rock. Recolour M_Rock_Under to warm beige/khaki strata (about #D2C29A / #B3A27A / #8E7F5E), drop the wave distortion to about 1.5 and use horizontal strata. Move SEA_Z to about -420. Move Cloud_CliffBase to z -110 to -170, halve the count, and leave gaps so the cliff silhouette shows in every island shot.

issues.issue: The lake and waterfall read as a swimming pool with a tree stump. The lake is a 48x26 m ellipse with only 3 m of wobble (layout.py 270, world.py 216). It sits inside a raised 7 m 'beach' terrace (Lake_Shore, z + 0.4 down to -1.0) whose stone side shows on the near shore (Region_SnailHuntingGrounds, right; SnailHuntingGround2 Overview, top right). The water has high-contrast thick white stripes. The source is Mountain_Mesa_A (terrain.py 76-82), a dirt-banded cylinder scaled 22x18x28 m with a grass dome, and the fall is a 10 m-wide sheet. In the reference the fall drops from a high rock outcrop backed by peaks.
issues.fix: Lake: wobble 10-15 m with 2-3 lobes. Sink the water 1.5-2 m below the surrounding ground with sloped grass banks, and keep sand to 2-3 short beaches (no raised retaining terrace). Lower the stripe contrast and add a shore-to-centre depth gradient (turquoise to deep blue). Waterfall: replace the mesa with a 60-80 m-wide rocky cliff wall (M_Mountain_Rocky or the new beige cliff rock) that merges into the NE massif peaks behind it. Make the fall about 40-50 m tall and 14-18 m wide, in two tiers with a splash ledge, plus a larger mist cluster. Optionally add an outflow stream south-east toward Rainbow Street with a small bridge, to tie the lake into the route.

issues.issue: The main route is not legible at island scale. Trails (world.py trails()) are 4.2 m dirt ramps in the same brown as in-map side paths. Inside maps, main-path widths and materials vary. In Island_Overview the Maple Road (MT, SHG I-III, fork, Southperry) and Rainbow Street (fork, Field West, Amherst, Field East, Tomato) cannot be traced without the debug labels and magenta routes. The world map's defining feature is a continuous pale road.
issues.fix: Add a shared 'main road' surface: pale cream/sand (close to the world-map road colour), 5-6 m wide, used for every Maple Road and Rainbow Street trail and exposed in MapCtx (e.g. m.main_path(points)), so map authors use it for the through-route between edge portals. Keep the branch trails to forests and gardens (in00-in05 etc.) narrower, in darker dirt. Clear trees within 8-10 m of main-road trails (Keepout segment radius is currently 6 m) so the road shows through the canopy.

issues.issue: Mushroom Town, the island's most iconic landmark, is under-developed (this applies to 20000 as well). Each map has only about 3-4 mushroom houses with caps of about 5-6 m, spread across large empty lime lawns (MushroomTown_10000_Overview: the middle and bottom halves are mostly bare grass). Filler-tree canopies are as large as the caps. In Island_Overview and Island_Hero the town is a few coloured dots at the NW tip, not the cluster of big mushroom houses the world map shows.
issues.fix: Put 6-8 mushroom houses per map, clustered along the main path in pairs and triples at different terrace heights, with caps scaled 1.4-1.8x (8-10 m) so they beat tree canopies. Add one tall landmark (a 14-18 m giant mushroom house or a 'Mushroom Town' arch over the path at the 10000/20000 seam). Give the core a packed-dirt or cobble plaza with lamps and a well. In world.scenery(), keep filler trees at least 15 m from the 0/10000/20000/30000 footprints so the town shows from island cameras.

issues.issue: Mountains don't frame the geography. Peaks come from a random scatter (world.py 364-412: up to 90 tries, keepout and occlusion rejection), which leaves sparse isolated cones. There is one tall peak behind Mushroom Town, a cluster NE of Amherst, and assorted medium cones on the front rim. The NW pocket ring, the ridge between the valley and the lake, and the NE massif north of the lake (worldmap.md section 2) are all missing. The iso camera looks toward geo +y (north), so tall scenery hides ground to its north.
issues.fix: Author ridge polylines in layout.py (RIDGES) and place peaks along them with height profiles instead of a random scatter. (1) NW pocket ring west and north of maps 0/10000/20000 (geo x -40 to 130, y 20-80): tall Mountain_Peak_Rocky with halos. These are behind the maps, so they cause no occlusion. (2) NE massif along the new north rim from about (300,-60) to (650,-110): tall. (3) A low ridge (10 m or less, Mountain_Hill or Peak_C) between SHG II/III and the lake, at least 15 m south of the shore so it doesn't hide the water. (4) South and SW rim: only rounded hills of 8 m or less, because of occludes_map.

issues.issue: Cloud_PeakRing puffs are half-buried in the mountain slopes and read as white lumps or snow blobs stuck to the flanks, not halos (Region_AmherstArea, peaks at upper right around (990,20), (1050,310), (1370,285); Region_RainbowStreet, upper right; Region_MapleRoad around (390,420)). From the code (world.py 405-410): puffs sit at radius 0.35*rad and height 0.72*h, scale 2.2. With the _peak profile the cone's surface radius at that height is only about 0.26*rad, so each 3 m puff is roughly half inside the mesh.
issues.fix: Put halo puffs at radius 0.26*rad + puff_radius + 2 m (about 0.5*rad). Use 8-10 puffs per ring at scale 3-4, flattened (z 0.5), forming a continuous ring like the world map's halo. Alternatively, add a thin white torus 'halo ring' asset. Limit halos to the tall Rocky peaks in the NW pocket and NE massif, since the reference rings only a few peaks.

issues.issue: The forest filler is a uniform carpet. There are 1165 trees in a Poisson-disc scatter (cell 5.5 m, world.py 435-466), with the palette taken from the nearest map. Orange and yellow birches dominate the valley and east palettes, which produces a speckled noise over the whole island (Island_Overview). There are no meadows or clearings and no dark forest masses, and trees run to the cliff edge everywhere. Map interiors are mostly bare flat lime grass, so contrast and hierarchy are inverted: busy surroundings, empty playfields. The build placed 1165 trees against a 2600 target, so raising density toward the target would make this worse.
issues.fix: Mask density with low-frequency noise (about 0.01/m). Aim for roughly 50% dense groves (scale 1.2-1.6, darker greens, tight spacing so they read as masses), 25% open meadow (flower and grass-tuft scatter, no trees) and a tree-free 6-10 m rim strip with occasional cliff-edge rocks and bushes. Cap autumn birches at about 15% outside the 'east' region. Use pines and tall trees in the 'forest' region north of Field West so the West Amherst forests read as a forest from above.

issues.issue: One M_Grass (bright lime) covers Island_Ground, every plinth and the ground of all 25 maps. Combined with the shared terrace language, SHG I-III, Field West, In a Small Forest, Mid Forest I/II and Dangerous Forest look alike in Overview shots. There is no regional ground tint to separate Maple Road, the Mushroom Town pocket, the Rainbow Street forests, Amherst and the SE fields.
issues.fix: Add 4-5 grass variants to the materials RECIPES: Mushroom Town fresh lime (the current one); valley warm yellow-green; West Amherst forests deep blue-green; Amherst gardens soft mint; SE fields golden-green. Map each street/region to a variant (extend region_of in world.py) and use it in plinth(), Island_Ground (via a vertex-colour or attribute mask blended across region borders) and the MapCtx default ground style.

issues.issue: Every island shot has a hard-edged dark navy wedge over the lower-left 25-35% of the frame (Island_Overview, Island_Hero, Island_WorldMapStyle), so it looks like two different waters. This is probably the island's cast shadow on the sea plane: sun from (1,-0.72,1.2) (scene_setup.py 78) at SEA_Z -260 gives about 270 m of offset. Confirm by disabling sun shadows on the sea, since the M_Sea noise ramp (materials.py 504) could add to it. The light-blue mottled sea also reads as sky, and the flattened Cloud_SeaLayer puffs (scale 18-34 x 14-26 x 5-9 at z -180 to -215) look like ice floes on water. The reference draws no sea surface, so this choice should be made deliberately.
issues.fix: Pick one concept. Option (a), a 'sky island': drop the hard sea plane for a soft cloud sea or a vertical gradient. Option (b), a real sea: deeper teal with a visible wave pattern and distance fog. In either case, stop the island shadow landing on it: make M_Sea mostly emissive/unlit, or use EEVEE light/shadow linking to exclude the sea from Sun_Key shadows. Make the sea-layer clouds puffier (z scale at least 0.5x of xy) and use about half as many.

issues.issue: Island scenery costs more than all the maps together: total 11,674,416 triangles, map sum 5,191,933, so about 6.48M are non-map (filler trees, cones, cloud puffs at subdiv 2-3, plinths). Only map 1000000 is flagged over budget, but the world layer is the real cost.
issues.fix: Add low-poly LOD variants for World_Forest instances (300-800 triangles per tree: merged canopy blobs, no inner spheres). Lower cloud puff subdivision to 1, cap puffs per cloud at 5, and use fewer, larger clouds. Report world-layer triangles as their own budget line in validation_report.json.

issues.issue: Trail geometry reads as framework scaffolding. Two long descents sit just under the 28° stairs threshold (30000 to 40000: 30 m, -11.9 m, 27.3°; 40002 to 50000: 32 m, -12.7 m, 26.9°), so they render as long brown slide-like chutes (Island_Overview around (410,230) and (760,420); Region_SnailHuntingGrounds, top left). The long side trails (1000000 to 1000005: 58 m; to 1000006: 64 m; 1010002 to 1010004: 46 m, +12.8 m) are ruler-straight ramps cutting through the stacked terrace bands (Region_WestAmherstForests, the three vertical brown strips).
issues.fix: In world.trails(), lower the stairs-or-switchback threshold to about 20°, and add a flat landing every 4-5 m of rise. Route trails longer than 25 m as curved polylines (Catmull-Rom through 1-3 waypoints that follow plinth edges or contours) instead of straight p1-to-p2. Add rope bridges where a trail crosses a gully between plinth stacks.

issues.issue: Dangerous Forest is as bright and cheerful as In a Small Forest and Mid Forest I. It has lime grass, orange and yellow birches, flowers and sunny clearings (DangerousForest_1000002_Overview). Nothing signals danger, and from the island it can't be told apart from its neighbours.
issues.fix: Use a darker tier palette: dense dark pines and bare or dead trees, thorn vines on the cliff faces, mushrooms instead of flowers, a few dark rocks and bones, plus a deeper blue-green grass variant once regional grass exists. In world.py, override the filler palette within about 25 m of 1000002 to pines and Tree_Tall only, so the block reads darker from Island_Overview.

issues.issue: A Split Road is the island's hub (the fork between Southperry and Rainbow Street), but at island scale it reads as just another stepped grass block. The fork is a slight widening of the path with knee-high signs (ASplitRoad_50000_Overview, right third), and it is not identifiable in Island_Overview.
issues.fix: Widen the junction into a small plaza (8-10 m) at the east00/east01 split. Add a tall multi-arm signpost (4-5 m) pointing to Southperry and Amherst, plus a bench and lamp. Make the Southperry branch visibly descend toward the lighthouse. With the shared main-road material, both branches should read as a Y from the island cameras.

issues.issue: 30 of the 80 itemised floating-prop issues are Rock_Cliff_Stone instances. These are cliff studs placed deliberately on vertical faces, by geo.py 438-455 and by map modules via m.place('Rock_Cliff_Stone', z=...). The floating check casts rays straight down, so it reports false positives that bury real floaters such as the 6.6 m-gap X1010001_Eave_4m.
issues.fix: Exempt assets tagged 'cliff' from the downward-ray check, or ray-test them horizontally against the nearest cliff face (pass if the gap is under 0.3 m). Keep the check strict for everything else so real floaters stand out.

verdicts.strengths: Reads clearly as the classic first map. The orange yellow-spotted mushroom house with its barrels and lantern sits on the spawn plateau, and its door faces the spawn. Heena stands on a big round bush above the spawn point. The three-step descent curls around the plateau corner, so it reads as terraced depth rather than a straight staircase. The laundry bluff has a camera-facing ladder face, Sera, two clotheslines, baskets and berry bushes. The 'climb here' mushroom cluster sits at the ladder foot. The front edge is kept low and the composition is clean. The trail to 10000 leaves the lane end sensibly.

Roger's raised hedge-walled garden is a good 3D translation: a display-only terrace with a hedge face to the street, vegetable beds, a scarecrow, and Roger visible from the street. The meadow sits low and a ramp climbs to the raised street, which keeps the classic tier rhythm. The main street path is clear and exits sensibly toward 20000.

All four classic landmarks are present and distinct. (1) The orange two-storey house has a stone arch over its door portal. (2) The stone oven tower has a little arched door, a log pile and a barrel flue, and out00 sits right beside it. (3) Nina sits on a giant mossy stump, a smart grounded version of her floating islet. (4) The sky islet is the grass-crowned cap of a giant red amanita with a ladder up its rim. The landmark pair reads as a skyline from the camera, and the south-face double stair is a sensible fix for the camera-hidden west risers.

A charming cut-away of Sen's two-storey mushroom house. The orange cap shows in cross-section over cream half-timbered walls. The railed loft holds the bed, curtained window and treasure chest, and the ladder reaches it through a railing gap that acts as the hatch. Downstairs there are a cupboard, a stove with a pot, bell lamps, a mushroom dining set and Sen. The door with its stone frame is on the west wall, as in the data. It reads well and is the most polished map in the region.

Most landmarks are present: the yellow house with its mushroom dormer, tall pale stalk mushrooms at the hill and at the summit, the rainbow mushroom fountain, ivy signposts including the three-arrow sign, the log bench, and Peter guarding out00 on the summit. The switchback-into-depth concept (valley in front, mid band, stepping stones at the back) is the right translation. The red and orange giant mushroom-cap stepping stones are a strong, whimsical touch, and the climb reaches a real 9.1 m.

issues.issue: The map's core identity, the 'climb to Peter' platforming, is lost. The data's floating islets (60 px hops with 12 px gaps, 236 px rope pitches) became abutting, near-identical rounded_rect grass blocks: Shelf_E1 (31.4-38.8 x 12.2-17), Shelf_E2, Ledge_E3 (24.4-31 x 16.4-25.6) and Ledge_M1 (18-25 x 16.6-26.4). They are separated only by 0.44 m curb steps. In the Gameplay render they read as one stepped massif, a staircase of identical slabs, and the AUTHORING 'not stacks of identical rectangles' rule is broken. No path ribbon continues past the fountain (Valley_Path ends at 34.4,10.2), so without the debug overlay the order (ropes east, hop west along M, ladder, stones east, summit) is invisible. The two rope pitches are only 2 m tall each (E1=2.0, E2=4.0). In the overview (about 860-880 x 690-800) they read as short knotted posts on the block lips, not ropes hanging down a cliff.
issues.fix: (1) Paint dirt path ribbons along the whole climb. Run the Valley path to the rope foot at (35.4,11.2). Add E1 lip to rope 2 at (33.6,14.8). Run E2 to E3 to M1 to the Slope_M2 foot. Run along M3 west to the U1 ladder foot at (8.8,24.6). Run U4 to S1 to Slope_S2. (2) Give each hop ledge a distinct organic or notched outline, a different footprint size, and a visible 0.3-0.6 m gap or plank/stone 'hop' bridge between blocks, so each reads as a separate islet or ledge. Use rock-pillar or stump styling for E1/E2, as AUTHORING section 1 suggests. (3) Make the rope faces read as cliffs. Hang the rope from a short wooden beam overhanging the lip, use a light hemp colour against the dark dirt, and cut a shallow notch or ledge in the face. Consider E1 about 2.6 m and E2 about 5.0 m so the two pitches dominate the low hops. (4) Put a small arrow sign at each switchback (E2 pointing west, the M3 west end pointing to the ladder, U4 pointing east).

issues.issue: Seam where a ramp meets the terrace above. The upper end of each m.ramp disappears under the upper terrace's rounded grass lip. What you see is a dirt sheet ending at a grass band, plus a detached thin dirt sliver (the ramp's flat end extension) on top of the upper terrace. Seen at 10000 Ramp_Meadow_Street (local x about 11-12.5, y about 12; overview about 490-610 x 510-570; Gameplay 100-180 x 345-480, a thin strip separated from the street path by grass). Also at 30000 Slope_M2 (x 16.6-19.8, y 21.2; overview about 780-860 x 455-520) and Slope_S2 (x 27.8-30.8, y 31). The 10000 module already follows the AUTHORING 'reach about 0.5 m inside the upper edge' rule, so this is a defect in the shared code, not an authoring mistake. The ramps read as cardboard sheets and break the route at exactly the points where it changes tier.
issues.fix: In mapkit, have ramp() notch the upper terrace's cap lip where the ramp lands (trim the cap outline or lower the lip locally), and blend the ramp top flush into the cap surface. Alternatively, auto-drape a path ribbon from the ramp's last segment about 1.5 m onto the upper cap. Module-level workaround until then: end each ramp about 1.5 m inside the upper outline and start the upper path ribbon on the ramp. For 10000, end the ramp at (13.0,12.8) and start Street_Path at (10.8,12.4). For 30000, start the M3 ribbon at x=18.5 and the Summit_Path at x=30.0.

issues.issue: The inter-map trail from the 30000 summit (out00) to 40000 is one straight ramp: 30 m long, -11.9 m, 27.3 degrees (build_report trails). It runs on a sheer knife-edge earth embankment. In the 30000 overview (about 1130-1450 x 560-900) and the bottom-right of Region_MushroomTownArea it reads as a giant brown wedge with vertical dirt walls. It starts right at the summit cliff lip, beside out00. layout.py marks it as intended ('long stair-ramp down from the East Entrance summit'), but it is the most artificial-looking element in the region, and a 27 degree straight slope undercuts the reward of reaching the summit.
issues.fix: In world.py/layout, build long, high-drop trails as switchbacks or stepped stairs with flat landings that hug a grassy hillside, and give the embankment sloped grass sides with trees and rocks instead of vertical dirt walls. Alternatively, cut the drop: raise the 40000 base z or lower the 30000 summit (the anchor hint was 7.0; the module raised S3 to 9.1) so the slope is 15 degrees or less. Keep a short flat summit apron (3-4 m) past out00 before the descent starts.

issues.issue: The classic 10000 landmark is a yellow mushroom house with a brown-streaked cap and a barrel chimney. The module places the generic v1 'House_Mushroom_Yellow' at (33.5,28.5): white-spotted cap, grey stone box chimney, no mushroom awning door, and smaller (cap_r 3.0, stem_h 2.8). kit/classic.py already has 'House_Mushroom_YellowStreaked' (streaked cap, collar, barrel chimney with yellow lid), whose docstring names 'Mushroom Town 10000'. The v1 style is also inconsistent with the v2 houses in maps 0, 20000 and 30000.
issues.fix: Swap to m.place('House_Mushroom_YellowStreaked', 33.5, 28.5, rot=-8). Optionally move it to about (30.5,27.5) so its west side nearly touches Roger's garden (x=27), as in the brief, and the cap reads beside the hedge garden.

issues.issue: Invented extra houses blur the two town screens. 10000 adds House_Mushroom_Blue (6.5,28) and House_Mushroom_Orange (40.5,36.0; y=36 is the footprint edge D, required=False). 20000 adds House_Mushroom_Blue (3.8,32) and House_Mushroom_BlueCone (37.8,32.8). The orange house in 10000 stands in the same frame as 20000's orange Sen's house (10000 overview right edge; 20000 overview top-left), diluting the only enterable landmark. Both town overviews now show the same blue, orange and yellow domes. Both extra blue houses are old v1 assets (stone box chimneys, no awnings), and 20000's background houses at scale 0.62-0.66 have doors about 1.2 m tall, shorter than the 1.5 m player.
issues.fix: Delete the House_Mushroom_Orange line in 10000. In 10000, replace the blue house with something 10000-specific (Roger's tool shed, a well, or the sunflower meadow expanded onto the back lawn). In 20000, keep at most the BlueCone and raise it to scale 0.85 or more; drop the v1 blue house or switch it to a v2 variant. The town distinction should come from each map's own landmark.

issues.issue: The west climb is cluttered and confusing. The two 'shortcut' plank flights (Steps_Lawn_T2 at x 11.5-14.2, y 14; Steps_T2_T3 at x 16.4-19.2, y 15.4) have risers facing away from the camera, so they render as flat plank pads lying on the grass (overview about 600-770 x 495-560). Lamp posts (15.0,11.8) and (19.8,13.4), two fence runs and Sign_Board (21,12.6) crowd round them. Meanwhile the main route makes a U-detour from in00 south to the front edge (y about 0.1) and back north up the double flight. In the debug overview the route and the dirt paths form a hairpin with two parallel climbs. The classic 'step up west to east' becomes unreadable at the point where the player arrives.
issues.fix: Remove both west flights with their lamps and fences, or replace them with a single ramp from the lawn at (11,14,0) rising north-east to (18.5,16,2) so the slope is visible. Keep the south double flight as the one climb, shorten Verge_Path so it heads directly from in00 to the verge flight foot, and move the Sign_Board to that foot (about 21.5,1.5). That leaves one clear lawn-to-street climb and frees the corner for clover beds.

issues.issue: Portal_Door (kit/markers.py) is a floor ring plus three stacked glowing discs up to 1.5 m high. In the beauty renders it reads as a solid cyan 'snowman' blob standing in the doorway, covering the bottom half of the door. It appears in front of the 20000 stone arch (Gameplay about 1160-1210 x 340-420) and in front of the 20001 west-wall door (Overview about 525-560 x 520-580; Gameplay 380-430 x 510-610), hiding the landmark door it marks.
issues.fix: Replace the vertical discs with a flat emissive threshold glow plus a thin emissive outline on the door frame, or a small floating chevron above the door at about 2.4 m. Keep markers below 0.1 m in front of door openings.

issues.issue: The town is sparse, not 'meaningfully more developed than fields'. The south half of the street terrace (x 12-42, y 3-12) is open lawn with only a fence, a sign and flower dots. The 12 x 10 m top of Roger's garden (15-27 x 24-34.5) holds only two small beds at its back plus Roger and a scarecrow. The house lot (26-40 x 22-35) is empty grass. Street furniture is just 2 lamps, 1 bench and a crate with a barrel. The Gameplay view (focus 24,17) frames mostly empty grass, with Roger and the house cut off at the edges.
issues.fix: Add the brief's vegetable fence (posts with a blue rope and leafy crops) along the garden's front top edge (y about 24.5-25.5), and more crop rows and a watering can across its top. Dress the house lot with a flower bed, a mailbox, firewood or a laundry tub. Line the street with 2-3 more lamps, planters and a second bench. Set GAMEPLAY_FOCUS to about (28,23) so the garden, Roger and the house fill the frame.

issues.issue: Door_Path ends at (33.3,22.8), but the house is at (33.5,28.5). Its door is at about y=26.8, so the path stops about 4 m short and ends in grass beside the crate and barrel (Gameplay 1400 x 480 vs the door at about 1460 x 320). The ToYellowHouse route stops there as well.
issues.fix: Extend Door_Path and the ToYellowHouse route to about (33.4,26.4), or to the door position of the YellowStreaked house after the swap. Move the Barrel/Crate at (30,22.5)/(29,23.5) beside the door instead.

issues.issue: The sunflower arrival meadow, one of the brief's recognizable beats, is weak. Seven small Sunflower_Patch are scattered over 1-10 x 1-20 with min_dist 2.2, and in the overview they are barely visible specks (about 360-420 x 560-600). The arrival from map 0 lands in a generic lawn.
issues.fix: Plant a dense sunflower bed flanking the in00 trail (x 1-8, y 5-15) at scale 1.3-1.6, leaving a 3 m corridor on Meadow_Path, and add a butterfly or two. It becomes the colour signature that distinguishes 10000 from 20000.

issues.issue: Every inter-map trail shows two full swirl portals 12-16 m apart: the out00 and the next map's in00 (0 overview 1115x700 and 1395x785; 10000 overview 160x455 and 385x500, 1100x690 and 1350x840; 20000 overview 1060x680 and 1200x800). In v8 the in00s are invisible arrival points (pt 1), and layout.ONE_WAY lists them. world.py line 307 computes one_way = (child, ca) in LY.ONE_WAY but never uses it, so arrival-only points get the same swirl as real exits. This is visual noise and implies a way back that the classic maps do not have.
issues.fix: Use the one_way flag in world.py/mapkit. Demote ONE_WAY arrival portals to a subtle ground ring, a 'Welcome to Mushroom Town' signpost or a wooden arch, or nothing. Keep a single swirl per link at the out portal.

issues.issue: The world filler around the maps is stacks of many thin contour-line terraces: 0.5-1 m striated dirt risers with grey stones, repeated 5-8 times. They fill the left third of the map 0 overview, the lower-left of the 10000 and 20000 overviews, the lower-left half of Region_MushroomTownArea, and the 30000 foreground. The result is a monotonous rice-paddy, topographic-map look that competes with the maps' real tiers, makes map edges hard to read, and adds dirt-face area without meaning. The smooth untextured olive cone 'mountains' framing the region also read as generic next to the puffy trees.
issues.fix: In world.py, generate filler slopes with fewer, taller, irregular steps, mostly grass-covered (sloped grass with occasional rock outcrops) rather than vertical dirt risers. Break them with tree clumps and bush bands. Give the cones some faceting or tree cover so they match the chunky hand-made style.

issues.issue: The first route of the game is fragmented. The path ribbons deliberately stop short of every stair: Plateau_Path ends at x 12.6 vs the stair top at 13.5; T3_Path ends at 20.2 vs the stair top at 21.0; Lane_Path starts at 23.9 vs the stair foot at 23.4; T2_Path is a separate patch. The descent reads as isolated dirt patches, grass gaps and big flagstone slabs (Gameplay 620-1050 x 370-900). The stone stairs have only 2-3 huge treads per 0.8 m rise, so they look like flat paving pads rather than steps.
issues.fix: Extend each ribbon about 0.3-0.5 m under the stair landings and feet (AUTHORING says ribbons now layer without z-fighting), so the dirt path flows into each flight. Use stairs with more, shallower treads (or a narrower width with chunky visible stone risers), and add a few rocks or flowers at each stair cheek so the steps read as steps.

issues.issue: Ladder and rope connectivity is never actually walked by the validator. Map 0 (ToBluffLadder/BluffTop), 20000 (ToSkyLadder/SkyIslet) and 30000 (Valley/RopeShelf_E1/MidBand/StonesToSummit/MeadowRecovery) split routes at every climb because of the old slope-window quirk, so build_report shows climb:0 for every route except 20001's Ladder. AUTHORING says the validator now stops the slope window at climbs.
issues.fix: Merge the split routes across their ladders and ropes in the three modules, e.g. one 30000 route from in00 to out00 through both ropes and the U1 ladder, and one map 0 route from the lane through the bluff ladder to Sera. Then the validator proves that the main climb connects.

issues.issue: The interior is a 16 x 12 m room with about 5 m walls, inside a house whose exterior stem in 20000 is about 4 m across. The classic room is about 5.4 x 3.5 m. The ground floor is a large open plank field with small furniture, so it feels like a barn rather than a cosy cottage. The all-orange and honey palette (floor, posts, rugs, crates) also makes props blend into the floor. The module follows AUTHORING section 8 ('roughly the size of the footprint', with L=16/D=12 fixed in layout), so this is guidance, not an authoring error.
issues.fix: Allow interiors to use a smaller room inside the stage footprint (e.g. 11 x 8 m for 20001). Add value and colour contrast: darker wainscot and floor trim, blue or green textiles on the bed and rugs, and a few cool-coloured jars. Fill the empty centre-left floor with the entry nook shelf, a coat rack or a hearth rug.

issues.issue: Clothesline_Laundry (kit/classic.py) is two straight posts and five flat rectangles. The brief's laundry has Y-shaped posts, a shirt, trousers, a white sheet on a sagging rope, and a butterfly on a post. On Sera's bluff (overview about 1050-1160 x 400-545) it reads as generic flags. Sera's tutorial bluff is one of map 0's four identity beats.
issues.fix: Upgrade the kit asset: Y-fork posts, a slight catenary rope, and cloth pieces with shirt and trouser silhouettes plus one long sheet, gently tilted as if in wind. Or define a local X0_Laundry in m0. Keep the two lines.

issues.issue: The two cut cap shells (back and left regions in mushroom_cap) meet at the apex with a visible V-notch and seam line (Overview about 735-760 x 190-230).
issues.fix: Overlap the two shell grids by one column or row at the corner, or add a small ridge cap piece along the corner seam.

issues.issue: The floating_props check flags wall-mounted assets as floating: Rock_Cliff_Stone embedded in cliff faces (14 in 30000, 6 in 0, 2 in 20000), plus X20001_WallShelf, RoundWindow, CurtainWindow and BellLamp in 20001. These false positives inflate the 245-instance count and hide real floaters.
issues.fix: Tag wall-mounted or hanging assets (cliff stones, vines, wall shelves, windows, lamps) in the kit and skip or face-test them in the validator.

verdicts.strengths: Strong whitewash-and-blue Mediterranean identity built from bespoke assets: the blue-domed house with Paul on its unreachable roof terrace (T21), the Armor Store with its scalloped blue roof, barrel chimney and pink arched door, the domed tower, the blue-capped lighthouse, Biggs's red-and-white gazebo, and a detailed three-masted <Victoria> with a gold/green strake, barrel engines and walkable decks. The classic five-zone structure is translated faithfully: the west square, the 2.5 m cliff with ledge T30, both ropes plus an added carved stair, the sunken street, the wide ramp, the belvedere reached by ladder x405 and by the slab-tower ladder plus stair, the knoll, the monumental grand stair (its risers face the camera), the quay, the gangplank, the decks and the mast rope. Every v8 NPC is in place. All 13 traversal routes pass and both portals link. The main route (square, west stair, street, ramp, grand stair, quay, gangplank) reads clearly in the Overview, and the town is clearly more developed than any field.

It is clearly the inside of the exterior Armor Store: whitewashed walls, a blue wainscot and the same pink arched door. Pan is plainly visible in an arched booth window, with helmets and shields on the back shelves and a green shield-cross sign. The classic climb survives in readable form: a varied heap of crates, barrels and boxes climbs to the wide shelf, and a rope leads to the blue-banded walkable beam, which matches the classic render cue, as do the stone-capped timber posts. Nautical touches (porthole, ship's wheel, lifebuoy, anchor, rope coils) tie it to the port. All 5 routes pass. The Gameplay frame is well filled, with the door, Pan, the heap and the shelf all in view.

issues.issue: The port town doesn't touch the sea or the island rim. ISLAND_MARGIN=34 m (layout.py) is applied uniformly, so Southperry sits about 34 m inland, boxed in by forest on all four sides. The 'harbour' is a sealed walled basin of about 26x16 m (Harbour water at x 54-80.4, y 22.6-39) on the town's back (+y) side, which faces inland toward A Split Road. Its water sits at WATER=3.45, which is above the upper street (Z_UP 2.2) and only 0.15 m below the knoll (3.6), so the ship reads as parked in a raised swimming pool on a lawn (see Southperry Overview, right; Region_SouthperryAndSplitRoad). In Island_Overview, Island_WorldMapStyle and Island_Hero the ship is almost invisible. The classic world-map signature (lighthouse plus airship hanging off the south cliff, worldmap_1_spots_annotated.png), which ITERATION_LOG R6 states as the intent ('Southperry on the south rim'), is lost. The town also reads as a rectangular stone slab dropped onto the meadow: straight retaining walls on the west, front and east, with forest planted right up to their foot.
issues.fix:
Two parts.
(1) Shared (layout.py/world.py): add a per-map rim override, e.g. MAPS[60000]['rim'] = {'front': 2, 'east': 2}, so the island outline hugs 60000's front (-y) and east (x=82) edges instead of the 34 m forest buffer. The quay front wall then becomes the island cliff dropping to the clouds (SEA_Z -260).
(2) Map: remove the back basin (Harbour, Breakwater, Garden_Breakwater, Parapet_Breakwater, Breakwater_Steps, Breakwater route).
- Re-moor the ship as a sky dock off the quay's front-right rim: hull centre about (76, -5), parallel to x, bow +x, running past x 82, so it is seen broadside like the world-map sprite and its sails hang over the void rather than over the street.
- Have it hover on its existing barrel engines, tied by ropes to Dock_Bollards on the quay lip, with the gangplank bridging from the quay edge at about (70, 3.5). Check with the Overview camera that the masts don't hide the quay.
- Move the lighthouse to the rim corner beside it.
- Reuse the freed back strip (x 54-80, y 22-46) for stepped whitewashed houses.
- Break the remaining straight plinth edges with rock outcrops and a stair down to the meadow.

issues.issue: The town's only edge exit can't be seen. west00 (layout anchor (8, 45)) lies directly behind the blue-domed house, whose footprint spans x 8.4-13.6, y about 35.8-44, with the dome finial at about z 10.7. It sits along this map's view direction (-0.375, +0.926), so no west00 beacon appears in the Southperry Overview, the Gameplay shot or the Region shot. In the debug Overview the RoadToSplitRoad route visually ends at the house wall, so arriving from A Split Road you enter behind a building. The module (comment at about lines 814-816) also admits the island trail's east rope rail at (8.99, 42.16) 'ends up wholly inside the house walls', which is a hidden intersection.
issues.fix: Move MAPS[60000]['anchors']['west00'] in layout.py to about (4.5, 45.0), in the visible gap between the CubeHouse (x about 1) and the dome house. The trail rails then fall at x about 2.2 and 6.9, clear of the house. Re-solve the layout. In the module, start ArrivalRoad at (4.5, 46.6) and update the RoadToSplitRoad route to match. Alternative: keep the anchor and move the dome house about 3 m forward (y 36.5) and 2 m east, then re-check that the bell wall is still visible.

issues.issue: Biggs's belvedere (Belvedere_W/E, x 16-44.6, y 30.3-46.6, z 8.2/9.0) is a solid mesa about 16 m deep. Its 5.5-8 m retaining wall forms one long blank grey masonry band across the whole back of the market street (Overview centre, Gameplay top edge). On top there is only a gazebo, 2 benches, 5 blue crates and some pots, roughly 400 m² of empty flagstone. The classic T12/T10 is a thin terrace floating above the shop roofs, not a plateau. Two other areas are also sparse: the quay east (x 62-82, y 5-22: two palms, an anchor, a few crates) and the west square's front half (x 0-15, y 2-18).
issues.fix: Cut the belvedere back to a strip about 7 m deep (y 30.3-37.5). Turn the area behind it into a lower stepped terrace of stacked Santorini houses (X60000_CubeHouse / DomeTower variants) with stairs. Dress the street-facing wall with arched doorways, blue-shuttered windows, flower boxes, more and thicker vines, and a whitewash (M_Plaster) band, rather than bare sandstone. Add cafe tables or a second canopy and laundry lines on the strip. On the quay, add a Shanks ticket booth or sign, a cargo net and a fish stall. On the square, add a fountain or well at about (8, 9) to anchor the arrival plaza.

issues.issue: The lighthouse annex is half scale. House_Stone_Port_2F at (45.9, 26.6), rot 12, scale 0.5 shrinks the asset's 6.4 x 5.0 m to 3.2 x 2.5 m, so its door and windows are about half the height of every other door in town (Gameplay top-right: its door is about half the lighthouse and dome-tower doors). Its teal shutters are off the town's blue palette. Its west side straddles the knoll lip at x about 44.2, above a 1.4 m drop to the upper street.
issues.fix: Replace it with a full-scale whitewashed, blue-roofed shed, the classic annex: either X60000_CubeHouse at scale 0.8 or a new X60000_Shed with a 1.9 m door. Place it at x 46.5 or more so it sits fully on the knoll. Don't scale door-bearing buildings below about 0.8.

issues.issue:
The Armor Store reuses the Amherst Weapon Store (m1010001) shell almost 1:1. Shared elements:
- the same camera, plank floor, stone-capped posts and banded eaves
- the door in the west wall at the front, the kiosk at the back-left, and the raised shelf plus rope in the back-right corner
- a round rug at the room centre
- a crate and barrel beside the door ((2.4, 1.2) / (3.3, 1.0))
- an Armor_Stand at (2.9, 5.3)
Side by side, the two Gameplay renders differ mainly in wall colour and in the heap versus the furnace.
issues.fix:
Keep the footholds but break the template:
- swap the plank floor for whitewashed stone flags or blue-and-white tiles that echo the town's flagstone
- replace the centred rug with an off-centre rope-bordered nautical rug
- replace the door-side crate, barrel and Armor_Stand with a fishing-net and lobster-pot corner
- hang a cargo net under the beam
- add a sea-view window with a light shaft on the back wall
- give the shelf a different form (ship-hull planking or a net-wrapped crate stack)

issues.issue: GAMEPLAY_FOCUS (34, 15) at scale 42 frames only the market street. Neither the ship nor the lighthouse is in the shot (only the lighthouse base shows at the top-right corner). About 20% of the frame (bottom-left) is the meadow below the town wall plus a cropped tree canopy, so the player-view screenshot is missing Southperry's two signature landmarks.
issues.fix: Move the focus to about (42, 18) and/or scale about 48, so the lighthouse, the foot of the grand stair and the topsails enter the frame and the outside lawn drops out.

issues.issue: The mast climb is truncated. The classic mast has three rope stages: deck to lower yard T2, to upper yard T1, to masthead T0 (the map's highest walkable point, about 1130 px above the quay). The module has a single MastRope to the fighting top at SHIP_TOP (deck + 8 m), with no upper stage and no crow's nest.
issues.fix: Add a second rope from MastTop up to a crow's-nest deck near the main-mast head (about WATER + SHIP_DECK + 16.5, radius 0.8, ring rail) and a ClimbMast2 climb_route. It makes a good vertical lookout landmark.

issues.issue: The classic slab stair (T22 to T19 to T17 to T13: four floating stone slabs, 60 px apart) became a solid whitewashed flight (SlabStair, x 42.8, y 32.8 to 39.4) on top of another blank block (SlabTower). It looks the same as the other stairs and loses the whimsical floating-slab read.
issues.fix: Render it as 4-5 thick open-riser stone slabs (about 1.6 x 2.6 m, 0.7 m rise) cantilevered from the belvedere wall, with visible gaps and shadow underneath. Keep the collision continuous using visible slab geometry, not hidden boxes. Add a whitewash band and a lantern to the SlabTower face.

issues.issue: The ArrivalRoad paving runs (7.6, 46.6) to (4.3, 32.3) to (1.0, 18.0) to (0.5, 15.8), ending at the pre-I3 portal site. It now dead-ends in the empty front-left corner of the square, while the real Main route turns east toward the WestStair. Its dark M_StoneWall band cuts diagonally across the square (Overview left). The comments at about lines 853-856 still say west00 is at (1, 18).
issues.fix: Together with the anchor move: aim the paving from the portal toward the WestStair head (16.6, 10.8) so it leads into the town's main axis, use a lighter or bordered paving so it doesn't look like a dark runway, and update the stale comments.

issues.issue: The two jibs and the spanker (the _flat_sail fans in the ship's x-z plane, built with recalc_normals=False) render as flat slate-grey shards next to the cream square sails (Overview: the large grey triangle at the bow, right of the fore mast). This is likely an unlit or back-facing side. Plausible, not confirmed.
issues.fix: Check that the fan normals face the camera (-y) or make the sail material shade both sides. Alternatively, angle the jibs about 20 degrees toward the camera, as the square sails are braced, so they catch the key light, or tint them slightly warmer.

issues.issue: The two classic ledge ropes (Rope_Street_Ledge_A/B at (17.8, 23.75) and (19.9, 23.6)) render as thick knotted wooden poles standing in the 2-4 m gap between the west cliff and the Armor Store (whose west wall is at about x 21.8). From the camera they sit partly under the store's roof (Gameplay top-left), so they read as posts, not climbables.
issues.fix: Add a visible beam or pulley at the top of each rope on the T30 lip and a coil at the foot. Shift the Armor Store about 1.2 m east (sx 26.5) to open a clear lane, and keep the ropes against the cliff face.

issues.issue: X60001_KnightArmor is placed three times ((13.15, 7.5), (9.7, 10.6), (10.6, 6.6)) alongside two Armor_Stands. The identical red-plumed suits form a copy-paste row across the right half of the Gameplay shot.
issues.fix: Keep one full suit, at (9.7, 10.6) by the shield rack. Replace the others with varied goods (a blue-tabard mannequin without a helmet, a boots-and-gloves rack, a chainmail stand), or vary the plume and tabard materials per instance.

issues.issue: Two classic walkable pieces are missing. The kiosk roof T5 (reached in the classic by jumping west from the beam's west end) has no deck: the striped awning slopes over it. The raised entry step T12 by the door is also absent, so the player spawns on the bare floor.
issues.fix: Add a walkable deck on the kiosk roof at about z 3.4 (move the awning under it, toward the back panel), reachable by a hop from the beam end at (3.35, 10.95, 5.0). Add a 0.45 m whitewashed entry step at about x 1.6-3.0, y 2.0-3.4, inside the door, and spawn the player on it.

issues.issue: ware_step() builds each heap step as a solid() collision box with hide_render=True (Heap_Crate_0..4, Top_Crate_A/B). These account for 7 of the validator's 12 'object hidden outside DEBUG' medium issues, i.e. all of this region's validator failures.
issues.fix: Either put collision proxies in a dedicated collection that is excluded from render and that the validator recognises (shared change in the validator and mapkit), or register the visible crate, barrel and box instances' tops as ground via m.add_ground and drop the hidden boxes.

issues.issue: The interior Overview shows the 16 x 12 m room in only about 40% of the frame, surrounded by empty blue, and the corner of a neighbouring interior pokes in at the top-right. INTERIOR_STAGE places interiors only 40 m apart (60001 at x 2440, 1010001 at 2480).
issues.fix: Increase INTERIOR_STAGE spacing to 80 m or more, or hide the other interiors while rendering one. Tighten the interior Overview ortho scale so the room fills about 70% of the frame.

verdicts.strengths: The stepped oval knoll is the clearest landmark in the region and reads at once: three concentric 1 m tiers with plank stairs, and you can walk round it. The terraces step back like an amphitheatre (ground, then mid, then upper) and read well from the iso camera. The main route (plateau, knoll, meadow, east00) is easy to follow along the dirt path. The autumn birch palette (orange and yellow canopies, white trunks) matches the brief. Mobs are Snail and Blue Snail only, as in the data. The east00 -> 40001 trail is a short 18.8 deg ramp that meets both portals squarely. The in00 arrival is spoiled by the shared steep-trail wall (see issues).

The most distinctive map in the region. The Arch Rock has a real see-through opening under its voussoir ring, and the stepping stones keep the classic arch-over-V silhouette (Λ over V). It is a whimsical, convincing use of 3D. White picket fences and the autumn grove at the entrance match the minimap. The ground route (west00, plank bridge, past the mesa foot, east field, east00) is obvious. The summit sits at the back-right with its camera-facing +x walls dressed. All 8 ropes exist and every rope route validates. Both trails (from 40000, to 40002) are short gentle ramps (18.8 and 9.5 deg) that arrive square to the portals.

The chimney gate is a good idea and it reads: two rock jambs with red banners and three stacked ledges with short ropes and a ladder clearly mark the only way up. The progression (front-left, back-left chimney, ridge, high back-right exit) uses depth well. The knoll is stepped on the west and faced on the east, as in the data. Red Snails are on the ridge and upper tiers. Faithful to the classic map, it shares 40000's west half, while the chimney and the bridge over the pit add some difference. The arrival from 40001 is a clean, gentle ramp.

The wide two-level road is translated faithfully. A long lower road runs along the front to Southperry (east01). The embankment and its crest lead to Amherst at the back-right (east00). The stepped mesa has its ropes, and the T9 and T10 rope blocks sit in front of the faces. Maria's raised flower platform, with its ladder and a custom red mailbox, is a charming touch. The custom 'Amherst' and 'Southperry' arrow boards help. In Region_SouthperryAndSplitRoad the two exits do head off in different directions. The east00 and east01 trails leave the map edge cleanly.

issues.issue: The two long inter-map trails are straight solid ramps with huge vertical walls. 30000->40000 (30 m, -11.9 m, 27.3 deg) and 40002->50000 (32 m, -12.7 m, 26.9 deg) both fall 1-1.5 deg under World.trails' `slope > 28.0` stairs cutoff. Each is therefore one geo.ramp with bottom=-2.0, which leaves a 12 m flat dark-brown wall facing the camera. You can see it in the 40000 overview at (150-400,130-430), the 40002 overview at (1230-1550,510-790), the top-left of the 50000 overview, and as brown slashes in Island_Overview_Close. The Trail_Rail fence pieces are placed flat at linearly interpolated z on a non-linear ramp profile, so they float or sink and read as isolated hurdles (40000 trail crop). This is the most visible artifact in the region.
issues.fix: In World.trails, pick stairs or switchbacks by rise (e.g. rise > 6 m), not by slope alone, and add a landing every ~3 m of rise. Build the bank flanks as stepped or sloped earth that tapers down to the plinth levels, with embedded rocks, instead of a bottom=-2 vertical wall. Sample each rail's z from ground_index and tilt each piece to the slope, or use one continuous rope rail.

issues.issue: traversal.clear_routes silently deletes authored landmark props. It removes any Trees/Foliage/Rocks instance within +-0.9 m of any route, including explicit m.place landmarks, and only logs them in build_report cleared_from_routes. The docstring says it only touches scattered clutter. Confirmed in the render: 50000 lost its brief-named mesa landmark (big Tree_Birch_Yellow). Also cleared: 40001 (2x X40001_Tree_Birch_Teal, 2x Tree_Birch_Orange, 2x Bush_C, Bush_A) and 40002 (Tree_Birch_Orange, Tree_Sapling_A, Bush_A, Bush_B).
issues.fix: Auto-clear only instances created by m.scatter (tag them at scatter time). Report m.place props that block a route as 'blocked' and make MAP_TRAVERSAL_OK False, so the author moves them. Print the cleared list in the build_map output.

issues.issue: The mesa landmark is missing. The big yellow tree (Tree_Birch_Yellow at (41.6,24.0), scale 1.35), which the brief names as the mesa's landmark, was removed by clear_routes because the Mesa_Rope502 route runs (38.8,25.6)->(43.0,22.0) through it. The high east top T3E (37.8-48 x 14.2-32.6) is now an empty lawn with one flower bed (overview (790-1060,320-560)).
issues.fix: Move the tree to about (44.8,28.5), at least 1.5 m from both the Mesa_Rope502 and Rope_2010_Trio routes, or bend the route via (40,27.5)->(43.5,21.5). Rebuild and check that cleared_from_routes is empty. Consider adding the brief's small red object on T3 next to it.

issues.issue: The fork does not read as a split road. The upper road can only be reached by Ladder_2095 (or by ropes and the mesa). Its dirt is a short, disconnected strip on top of the embankment (overview (1040-1530,535-600)), and the junction boards are at 0.6 scale. From the iso camera, east00 and east01 look like two portals at the right edge about 19 m apart, with no visible Y. The brief's 3D concept, 'the road forks in plan, not only in height', is not delivered.
issues.fix: Stage the junction at x 50-56 as a fork point. Put full-scale paired Amherst/Southperry boards at the ladder foot on the lower road. Add a short wooden stair or ramp up the embankment face beside ladder x2095 (2.2 m rise), keeping the ladder. Paint one continuous upper path from the ladder head to east00. Bend the lower road slightly toward the front-right after x 50 so the two branches visibly separate.

issues.issue: This is the only map in the region that fails traversal (traversal.ok=false). Move the teal birch grove onto T0's front half (y 39.5-41.5, x 32-48), at least 1.5 m from the Main_7 route at y~42. Add embedded rocks and vines to the 4.9 m ridge front wall. Frame east00 with a banner pair or rock gate matching the chimney banners.

issues.issue: The upper band (HighWest with the hump, the T0 islet spire, HighEast) is mostly hidden. issues.issue: The kit has no natural-rock terrace style, so maps use grass_stone (Amherst blue-grey flagstone masonry) for Maple Island rock. issues.fix: Add a `grass_rock` style to the kit: warm grey-brown irregular rock with a rounded, slightly tapered silhouette and embedded boulders. Switch these Maple Road terraces to it. Until then, use grass_dirt with Rock_Cliff_Stone embeds.

Make the arch-leg stones wider and rockier than the lintel stones. Shade the drum sides darker (rock style) so the caps stand out.

issues.issue: Ropes look like freestanding knotted posts. The rope asset is a thick knotted pole with a cap, standing 0.3 m off the face with nothing tying it to the ledge lip. issues.issue: T3_Ramp (x 33->37.5, y 25.6, width 3.6, top_mat=None) renders as a pale flat sheet with a dark side wedge between T3W and T3E. It reads as a floating panel (overview (755-880,365-410); gameplay top (460-720,30-80)).

issues.issue: CentralTerrace (21-47 x 18-28.5) is a large, mostly empty flat slab in the overview (680-1000,430-560). The brief's T10 dressing (an orange tree and a red-leaf tree with bushes at x~1000-1330 px, about local x 25-31) is reduced to one tree at (24,19.5).

issues.issue: AUTHORING.md section 3 has the sign wrong for world yaw -103 (40001). It says the view dir is about (+0.85,+0.5), so +x faces are hidden. verdicts.strengths: Verdicts in this review rate design and visual quality. Traversal failures are listed separately as high issues. Amherst reads clearly as the cobblestone town on three levels. The grey-blue stone bastion and plateau sit behind the west street, as the brief proposes. The paired rope and ladder (26.9/28.9, 19.1) are the only way up and are easy to read. The raised square has the lime Department Store (in02), the rainbow spring and two planters. The east street has the face cut-outs, the banner pole and the giant tree house at east00. The red mailbox and town gate sit at west00. The houses are distinct (yellow, red, Weapon Store, lime, orange plus the tree house), so the town is clearly more developed than the fields and is recognisable at island scale. In 3D the plateau-over-street overlap became real depth. Weak spots: the stair artifacts on the main street, the belvedere pillars, the striped 'balloon' caps, the empty front meadow, and the blocked in01 with a second orange house behind it.

A convincing forge workshop, not a generic shop. Sid's boarded booth is in the back-left with racks of swords. The back wall has the gear window and the chained armor alcove. The domed furnace has a glowing mouth, a stack pipe and the green-banded tank. A railed metal stair climbs to the scaffold deck, and a rope reaches the beam, so the classic climb is kept and readable. Materials and beams match the Department Store, so the two shops read as a pair. The route is clean and traversal passes. The only weakness is the small overview framing; there are no visible artifacts.

The doll-house cutaway shows both storeys at once: bookcase and rug downstairs, ladder up to the bed, chest and curtained window in the loft. The west door leads to the DANGER skull sign and west00, so the brief's through-route idea is there. Rated needs_work for more than the blocked west door: the map is mostly bare plinth grass, and the cap section reads like a projector screen. It also duplicates Amherst's orange house 12 m away at a different scale and style, and the SFoF trail joins it with hard rectangular slabs.

All classic landmarks are present: the WELCOME booth with the money-bag board, the POTIONS wall shelves, the 'Thank you' arched door with the portal, the pole shelf with jars as a spiral stair, the treasure chest high on the right wall, and the same shell and blue-lashed beams as the Weapon Store. It is warm and cozy, and traversal passes. Weaker than the Weapon Store: the spiral treads read as loose floating wedges, the shelf-hopping route is hard to follow, and the room fills only about a third of the overview frame.

Well crafted and full of identity details: the fenced, hedge-lined rim road at the back, green leafy vines down the rim face, three colour-coded meadows (purple irises, clover, orange marigolds) with dip stones, the orange-flower centre knoll, the round stone stair up the east side, butterflies, and Snail, Blue Snail and Red Snail only. The tiers step back cleanly. Rated needs_work because the brief's top identity point is inverted: the layout anchor puts east00 near the front, so you arrive at the bottom-right instead of on the rim looking down. The 0.8 m bowl barely reads, the four climbable vines are lost in a curtain of decorative strands, and six plinth rings and a 40 m straight trail make it sit on a 'wedding cake'.

The 10-row lattice became a hillside that climbs away from the meadow, with chains of round earth-pillar stepping stones, berry and clover shelves, and the crown at the back-west. The yaw-aware design is sensible. The hidden entrance is marked by the DANGER sign, three tomato plants and a fun giant-tomato barrel gate. Ladders and ropes sit on the faces, autumn trees surround it, and it is clearly distinct from the town. Issues: plank stairs read as loose boards, the path ribbon breaks into stripes over Ramp_West, the 'giant' mushrooms are small, and the dark trail embankment to the Tomato Field gives the hidden entrance away.

The strongest field identity in the region. Sunken beds hold staked tomato rows that run into depth, with scarecrows, crates of tomatoes and giant tomatoes. A wooden trellis boardwalk on vine-wrapped posts along the back translates the 17-platform canopy, reached by five vine ropes. A hedge-walled arrival bank sits under the tomato gate, gentle slopes replace steps, and mobs are on the ground only. The farm reads instantly and is unlike any other map. Issues: one blocked route (crates and scarecrow), triangular slope wedges along the front edge, blob-like haystacks, and the heavy arrival embankment.

issues.issue: Route ToTownstreet fails: it is blocked at (64.0, 38.8) by House_Mushroom_OrangeSpotted (geometry 0.36 m above the walk surface). The house is placed at (64.0, 41.3), straddling the back edge (D=40) and overhanging it by about 4 m, which breaks the 1 m overhang rule. Its stem fills the 4.5 m corridor in front of the in01 anchor (64, 39), and its cap covers the start of the world trail to Townstreet. The player has to walk into a wall to reach in01.
issues.fix: Move the house off the in01 corridor, e.g. to (58.6, 35.5) at rot=-60 so it faces the yard from the side, and keep a clear 4.5 m lane from (64, 32) to (64, 40). Put a small garden gate or arch at (64, 39.2) as the in01 marker. Better still, combine this with the shared fix below and drop the exterior duplicate entirely.

issues.issue: Two orange mushroom houses stand back to back. LINKS puts Townstreet out00 only 12 m behind Amherst in01, so the player enters Amherst's orange-spotted house and walks out 12 m later into a second, different orange house. Townstreet's cutaway is a 12.8 x 10 m ellipse, about 11 m tall, with a smooth cap and no yellow spots. Amherst's is about 6-7 m with a spotted cap. This is visible in Region_AmherstArea and Region_RainbowStreet, and it contradicts the brief ('Townstreet = the inside of Amherst's orange house').
issues.fix: Layout: cut the gap for (1010002, out00, 1010000, in01) from 12.0 to about 3-4 m. Amherst: remove the orange house from the in01 spot, so Townstreet's cutaway house becomes the orange house in Amherst's skyline, seen straight up the yard lane. Townstreet: give the cap Amherst's orange-with-yellow-spots material (M_Spot_mush_orange__flower_yellow) and a barrel-stack chimney so it matches the classic house6.

issues.issue: Route Main fails at (8.6, 9.9): it is blocked by X1010002_CutawayHouse at 0.45 m. The west doorway WEST_DOOR=(206 deg, 220 deg) is only about 1.4 m of arc on the 6.4 x 5.0 wall ellipse, narrower than the 2.6 m path rule. The route crosses through the frame or doorstep rather than a clear opening.
issues.fix: Widen WEST_DOOR to about (199, 227) deg, a clear opening of at least 2.6 m. Make the two doorstep treads (0.2 / 0.45) part of the ground index, or replace them with a single 0.4 m ramp. Route through the opening's centre: (12.0, 9.6) -> door centre -> (6.6, 10.2) -> (5.0, 11.2).

issues.issue: Route WestBed fails. On the (10.0, 15.2)->(14.2, 12.0) leg it hits X1020001_CratesTomatoes_05 at (11.4, 13.6), 0.43 m. The x=19 leg runs straight through the Scarecrow at (19.0, 8.2), 1.01 m.
issues.fix: Move the crate and sack to (12.6, 15.6) and (13.4, 15.9) on the bed's north edge. Move the scarecrow to (17.2, 8.0), between rows, or shift that route leg to x=19.8. Then re-run build_map until MAP_TRAVERSAL_OK is True.

issues.issue: The SFoF east00 anchor is at local (37, 10, 0), at the front-right, but the classic exit and arrival are on the top rim, 1200 px above the basin. The module docstring admits the workaround: 'The layout fixes the exit at the east edge near the front, so the road arrives there on a gate landing and climbs north'. The player therefore arrives at the bottom and walks up a 4 m dirt lane (EastLane 36,12 -> 36,28.6), which inverts the brief's top identity item ('you arrive at the top... look down into a flower-filled bowl'). Base z=18 also gives 6 plinth rings and a 40 m straight trail climbing about 12.8 m from Townstreet (z 8).
issues.fix: In layout.py set 1010004 anchors east00 -> (37.0, 31.5, 10.0), the east end of the rim road. Lower SFoF z from 18 to about 9-10, so the rim is about 19-20 m in world space and the trail from Townstreet climbs about 11-12 m over 40 m with a switchback or stair landings. Then delete GateLanding and EastLane from the module and use the freed east strip (33-38, 8-28) to widen the T15 east rim and the stone stair.

issues.issue: geo.stairs builds 0.16 m floating tread boxes with no risers or solid body, plus a 0.3 m-thick landing slab on top of the upper terrace. On stairs running along local x for yaw-0 maps (edge-on to the camera), the treads read as separate paving tiles with grass gaps. Examples: Amherst main street EastStairs_Upper/Lower (50.5-56.4, 11), Look_Stairs (48.4-51, 23.4), LedgeStep (29.6, 22.6-25.8), and the plank WestStep (23.4-25.9, 11), which also clashes with the cobble street. FEoA Stair_T23_Nook, Stair_Berry_Clover and Stair_T12_T18 read as loose boards lying on the grass, and their landings look like dropped planks.
issues.fix: Kit: build each step as a solid block from its tread top down to p0.z-0.3 with side_mat risers and cheeks. Make the landing flush and thin (top at p1.z+0.01, 0.06 thick), or skip it when p1 is already 0.5 m inside the terrace. Map workaround for Amherst: replace the street stairs with cobble ramps (0.8 m rise over 3 m or more, style='cobble') or orient them along y toward the camera. Use M_StoneWall for WestStep.

issues.issue: Trail-to-portal junctions show hard rectangular slabs. The trail's flat '_In'/'_Out' segments overlap map ground as straight-edged dirt aprons with a pale overlapping patch, and the trail turns 90 degrees right at the portal. Examples: Townstreet west00 (1, 12) (clearest, Overview x 290-480, y 600-660), Amherst east00 (75, 12) toward FEoA (pale square at FEoA Overview x 390-430, y 195-230), and the SFoF gate landing seam (Overview x 1230-1290, y 715-760).
issues.fix: In World.trails: clip the inside-map 1.2 m segment at the footprint edge and use path_ribbon draped on map ground instead of a solid ramp box. Fillet the perpendicular-exit corner with a curve of radius 4 m or more. Match the trail top to the map ground height at the edge, so no lip or double surface appears.

issues.issue: The FEoA in00 -> Tomato Field out00 trail drops about 7.4 m over 22 m (nook z 10.6 to TF z 3.2). It is drawn as a dirt embankment with a roughly 5 m flat dark-brown side face, the largest dark surface in both maps (FEoA Overview x 1160-1400, y 500-620; TF Overview top-left). It also announces the 'hidden' Tomato Field entrance from afar, and the identical tomato gates at both ends look copy-pasted.
issues.fix: Shared: for trails with more than 3 m of drop, build stair flights with grass landings set into a grass-capped cut (plinth-style terraces with rock faces and Rock_Cliff_Stone), or add a switchback. Line it with trees and hedges so the passage reads as secret. Layout: raise TF z (2 -> about 5) to halve the drop. Optional map change: on the FEoA side, hide the gate in a hedge tunnel and keep the giant tomato only on the TF side.

issues.issue: World.plinth stacks identical rings (STEP=3 m, margin +3.6 m per level), so high maps sit on striped 'wedding-cake' terraces. SFoF has 6 rings, filling the region between Dangerous Forest, Townstreet and SFoF with parallel bands (Region_AmherstArea centre-top, x 430-700, y 200-480). This reads as artificial and makes map borders ambiguous, because SFoF's own tiers use the same look.
issues.fix: Vary the ring step height (2-4.5 m) and the margin per side, wobble ring outlines more, and merge rings of adjacent maps into one hill mass. Give the lower rings rock-cliff faces, forest scatter and a few ramps. Lowering SFoF z (see above) also removes 3 rings.

issues.issue: The clover basin is only 0.8 m deep: T14/T15 rims at 0.8, banks T16/T17 at 0.4, floor at plinth 0. The front half (y 0-18) reads as flat grass strips with seams (Overview x 480/860/910), not the symmetric stepped bowl that is the map's lowest band. The bowl's west-east symmetry does not read in 3D.
issues.fix: Raise the whole tier stack by about 1.2 m and set the basin floor to a 0.3 m terrace. Put the rims at about 2.0 m and the banks at about 1.0 m, joined by short grass ramps or one stone step each side, so the front reads as a bowl. Curve the rim outlines inward (U-shape around x 6-24) instead of straight strips.

issues.issue: The four climbable rim vines (x 4.6/15.6/21.6/30.6) are lost among 18 Vine_Curtain strands, 5 Vine_MidFace strands and 2 dead-end vines of the same green. In Overview and Gameplay the rim face looks uniformly striped, so the player cannot tell which vines go down.
issues.fix: Cut the curtain to about 6 short strands (no more than 1 m) kept at least 2 m from LONG_VINES. Give the climbable vines a brighter leaf material and more flowers. Mark each fence gap at the top with a small arch or post with a leaf sign, and a light-coloured patch of path where the vine starts.

issues.issue: The T08-T10 belvedere is three bare grass-capped stone drums at (50-58, 21-34) joined by flat-tile stairs and a rope. It reads as the arbitrary floating platforms AUTHORING warns against. The brief proposes a wooden lookout tower.
issues.fix: Replace it with a timber lookout. Use m.deck for T08 at 2.4 m on posts and T09 at 4.8 m with a rail, with the rope between. Add a small roofed top (T10, 5.6) with a pennant using a local X1010000_Lookout roof. This gives Amherst's east corner a vertical landmark to balance the tree house.

issues.issue: The red mushroom tower (House_Mushroom_RedStriped, scale z 1.28, at 18.4, 21.0) and the yellow house (House_Mushroom_YellowStreaked, 9.6, 20.6) use striped caps. issues.fix: Build a local X1010000_RedTower with mushroom_house_v2: stem_h about 6 m with two rows of round windows, a smooth red cap with white spots (M_Spot_mush_red__mush_spot) and a pipe chimney. Use a smooth yellow cap and a green door for the yellow house.

issues.issue: The Weapon Store exterior (House_Wood_TwoStory_Capped at 12.5, 32.6) has no signboard with the green sword icon and no thatched annex. issues.fix: Add an X1010000_SwordSign, a copy of X1010000_PotionSign using _shop_sign(mb, 'sword', ...), at about (14.8, 28.8) facing -y beside in00 (11.3, 29.4). Add a low thatched lean-to annex on the store's east side at about (16.5, 32.5). Optionally scale the cap down or raise the stem so the window shows.

issues.issue: The cap section is a flat grey-beige half-disk with a strip of white rectangles, which reads as a projector screen or awning (Overview x 600-1150, y 230-360). The rest of the 24 x 22 m map is bare plinth grass: the east SideYard path is a dead-end to crates, and the west garden has a single flower bed. The brief's orange flower bed and bush are thin.
issues.fix: Give the cut face a warm cream 'flesh' gradient with radial gill grooves and a darker rim band, or show attic rafters. Dress the garden: an orange flower bed and bush cluster at (4-7, 13-17), a low hedge along both sides of GardenPath, and a trail-head arch with the DANGER sign at west00.
